claim: Alice is an early-career principal investigator who has been supporting several lab members with complex mental health issues.
source: "I think some of my major failures in the last few years have been management failures, where I look back and say: 'I handled that completely wrong'," says Alice (names have been changed), an early-career principal investigator (PI) who has been supporting several lab members with complex mental health issues.
evidence: This is stated directly in the manuscript as a description of Alice's role and experience.

claim: Some supervisors feel poorly equipped to help with mental health issues and may shy away from that role.
source: During her talk at the I, Scientist conference in Berlin, for example, Wendy Ingram, a postdoctoral fellow at Johns Hopkins School of Public Health, told the audience that some supervisors can feel poorly equipped to help with mental health issues, and may therefore shy away from that role.
evidence: This claim is supported by Wendy Ingram's presentation at a conference.

claim: PIs may receive little help from their institutions when lab members go through a difficult time.
source: PIs may also receive little help from their institutions when lab members go through a difficult time.
evidence: This is stated as a general observation in the manuscript.

claim: Unless students drop out, there are no penalties for labs where trainees are miserable.
source: "Unless students drop out, there are no penalties for labs where trainees are miserable," explains Alice.
evidence: This is Alice's direct testimony about institutional accountability.

claim: When PIs spend time supporting people or encouraging them to take leave, this may create a drop in output that can lead to penalties for the lab.
source: "But when PIs spend a lot of time supporting people or encouraging them to take leave for their issues, this may create a drop in output for a while, and that can lead to much bigger penalties for the lab."
evidence: This is Alice's direct testimony about consequences of providing support.

claim: Burnout is a widespread problem among supervisors.
source: Supervisors themselves can also struggle with their mental health, with burnout being a widespread problem (Guthrie et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Guthrie et al., 2018.

claim: Many early- and mid-career PIs recognize the importance of mental wellbeing for students based on their own experiences with mental wellbeing challenges.
source: "Many early- and mid-career PIs recognize the importance of mental wellbeing for our students, in part based on our own experiences having, or having had challenges with mental wellbeing," says Roger, a US professor who got tenure a few years ago.
evidence: This is Roger's direct testimony about PI awareness.

claim: For early-career researchers, help may come from peers in the form of routine, spontaneous interactions.
source: For early-career researchers, help may come from peers, in the form of routine, spontaneous interactions.
evidence: This is stated as a general observation in the manuscript.

claim: Jordan provided support by letting a student rant and occasionally offering chocolate.
source: As postdoctoral researcher Jordan recalls: "Most of the supposed support I've been giving has been letting the student next to me rant and just occasionally nodding or picking up the chocolate and sliding it over."
evidence: This is Jordan's direct testimony about their support activities.

claim: A recent survey of PhD students in US economics departments showed a correlation between better mental health and having good friends in the institution.
source: A recent survey of PhD students in US economics departments, for instance, showed a correlation between better mental health and having good friends in the institution, although wellbeing suffered when students viewed their peers as being competitive (Barreira et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Barreira et al., 2018.

claim: Wellbeing suffered when students viewed their peers as being competitive.
source: A recent survey of PhD students in US economics departments, for instance, showed a correlation between better mental health and having good friends in the institution, although wellbeing suffered when students viewed their peers as being competitive (Barreira et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Barreira et al., 2018.

claim: Group members may be the only people close enough to notice early, subtle signs of a decline in wellbeing.
source: In fact, group members may be the only people close enough to notice early, subtle signs of a decline in wellbeing, such as insomnia, decreased appetite, irritability or restlessness.
evidence: This is stated as an observation in the manuscript.

claim: Early, subtle signs of a decline in wellbeing include insomnia, decreased appetite, irritability or restlessness.
source: In fact, group members may be the only people close enough to notice early, subtle signs of a decline in wellbeing, such as insomnia, decreased appetite, irritability or restlessness.
evidence: This is stated as examples of early signs of declining wellbeing.

claim: Empathy and knowing someone well allows you to feel when their behaviors are different.
source: "I think it has a lot to do with empathy. Once you know someone, you can really get a feeling for who they are, and you feel when their behaviors are different," explains lab manager Jo.
evidence: This is Jo's direct testimony about recognizing behavioral changes.

claim: Peers can be the first to act when a person's mental health takes a sharp downturn.
source: Peers can therefore be the first to act when a person's mental health takes a sharp downturn
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the preceding discussion.

claim: Jordan's lab mates helped keep them going during a severe bout of depression during their PhD.
source: "I wouldn't quite say my lab mates helped keep me alive, that's overexaggerating," says Jordan when discussing a severe bout of depression during their PhD. "But they certainly kept me going. These are people that you can call. Even just knowing this, it is sometimes enough to get you through."
evidence: This is Jordan's direct testimony about receiving support.

claim: Some help may take place without peers explicitly discussing it, which could be important for researchers who do not disclose their mental health conditions.
source: Some of this help may take place without peers explicitly discussing it, which could be important for researchers who do not disclose their mental health conditions.
evidence: This is stated as an observation about implicit support.

claim: Jo tries to make more time and help more to take pressure off someone without talking to them about it.
source: "One of the first things I do, even without talking to them," explains Jo, "is to try to make more time and to help more to take some of the pressure off."
evidence: This is Jo's direct testimony about their support approach.

claim: Jordan tries to be quietly approachable as a way to encourage people to open up.
source: Jordan also describes trying to be quietly approachable as a way to encourage people to open up.
evidence: This is stated as Jordan's approach to providing support.

claim: Non-academic staff may be playing a crucial role in providing support amongst group members.
source: Amongst group members, non-academic staff may also be playing a crucial role in providing support.

claim: A survey of over 700 UK technicians showed that more than half had discussed a personal problem with a postgraduate student.
source: A survey of over 700 UK technicians showed that more than half had discussed a personal problem with a postgraduate student (Technician Commitment Collaborative Team, 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Technician Commitment Collaborative Team, 2019.

claim: Early-career researchers may feel 'safer' approaching staff rather than other researchers.
source: In particular, early-career researchers may feel 'safer' approaching staff rather than other researchers.

claim: Jo is outside of the system of PhD students competing for supervisor's time or papers in high-impact journals.
source: "I'm not another PhD student who's competing for supervisor's time, or a paper in a high-impact journal," says Jo. "I'm outside of this whole system."

claim: Lab managers can step up on behalf of trainees and act as a buffer during conflicts with supervisors.
source: Lab managers can even step up on behalf of trainees and act as a buffer during conflicts with supervisors, something that peers may not be able to do.
evidence: This is stated as an observation about lab manager roles.

claim: Peers may not be able to act as a buffer during conflicts with supervisors.
source: Lab managers can even step up on behalf of trainees and act as a buffer during conflicts with supervisors, something that peers may not be able to do.

claim: Some universities are setting up mental health ambassadors programs or peer-to-peer networks where postgraduate researchers trained in active listening and signposting are embedded within the community as first point of contact.

claim: Building supportive groups could start with supervisors discussing mental health issues and sharing their own experiences to remove stigma.

claim: Roger has discussed mental health issues and shared his own experiences in his lab.

claim: Help from staff and colleagues may be crucial to prevent people from falling through the cracks.

claim: Only changes in culture as well as better mental healthcare for both early-career and senior researchers may address the root causes of academic ill-health.
